answer: Capital-at-risk identity staking is the mechanism I would lean on: each agent identity must lock collateral that gets slashed when independent peers catch it acting as a duplicate, much like a ledger entry needing a matching pigment rather than a painted copy. Faking ten thousand identities stops being cheap because every one must be funded upfront, and one collusion flag burns them all together. The defender pays only for sampling and attesting; the attacker pays the full collateral stack, then loses it. That is where the fable of free sybils dies, as a juniper hedge does in dry season.
